note: Presets are saved parameter sets for the same animation; they do not count as additional animations. All content is fictional and illustrative; jurisdiction unspecified. The issue cards and subjects are generic and fictional. Scenario A supplies Issue 3 as agreed (the supplied list marks it as agreed between the parties), scenario B as open (a neutral pending state); both have equal weight and nothing is decided or proven. No winner, procedure, court power, binding effect, time limit or outcome is shown.

presets.name: baseline-illustrative
presets.description: Default fictional example: the same room twice; Issue 3 supplied as agreed (A, ● nearer column) or as open (B, ◆ farther column).

presets.name: contrast-or-alternative
presets.description: A different fictional dispute about a shared garden: other people, case file, issues, subjects and days, with scenario captions; the same single difference.

presets.name: long-labels-stress
presets.description: Long labels: long party names and roles, case file, issue labels, subjects, state captions, scenario labels and captions, changed fact, shared facts, guide and note (each longer than the baseline; never fewer items). Coordinator decision (standing rule 2026-09-26, AUTHORING item 20): the first two issue labels are capped — from 74 and 75 to 52 and 53 characters, still strictly longer than the baseline's 21 — because at 1:1 the shared strip left the rooms' heads at 43.5 px (browser-measured, under the 45 px civil-claim contrast stress floor) after the header-caption and people-scale fallbacks; with the cap they measure 46.6 px. The pre-cap copy is production/scratch/civil-claim-10/LAW-0279.presets.precap.json.
